title: Say it louder
prompt:
Print every command-line argument in capitals, one per line, each followed by `!`. With `quiet please` in the args box the program prints `QUIET!` and then `PLEASE!`.

`main` receives the argument count in `w0` and the address of `argv`, an array of 8-byte pointers to strings, in `x1`. Entry 0 is the program's own name, so start at entry 1. With no arguments the program prints nothing at all.

Walk each argument's bytes with `ldrb` until the terminating zero. Only the bytes from `'a'` to `'z'` change: in ASCII each lower-case letter sits exactly 32 above its capital. Digits, punctuation, and letters that are already capitals stay as they are. You can write each changed byte back into the argument with `strb` and then print the whole string with the format in `.data`.

## what is checked

- the shouted lines for the arguments in the args box, and for more arguments you cannot see
- the program exits cleanly
- the bytes are read one at a time (`ldrb`)
starter:
// shout every command-line argument: upper case, one per line, with a !
define(fp, x29)
define(lr, x30)

define(nargs_r, w19)
define(args_r, x20)
define(i_r, w21)
define(ptr_r, x22)

.data
fmt_shout:  .string "%s!\n"

.text
        .balign 4
        .global main
main:
        stp     fp, lr, [sp, -16]!
        mov     fp, sp

        mov     nargs_r, w0
        mov     args_r, x1

        // TODO: for each argv[i] from i = 1 up to argc - 1, change every
        // letter from 'a' to 'z' into its capital, leaving every other
        // byte alone, then print the argument with fmt_shout.

        mov     w0, 0
        ldp     fp, lr, [sp], 16
        ret
